notes:
Account background: Verdigris Sentinel is a payments/identity risk team inside a large financial institution. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated to replace a mix of in-house Triton endpoints + bursty cloud GPUs. Primary asks: reproducible throughput guarantees for peak-shopping windows, tight p95 latency SLOs for chat (human-in-loop), and clear reserved-GPU planning + billing for warm capacity.

POC scope and success criteria:
- Throughput target: sustained 800 requests/sec (512-token avg) at p95 <= 180ms end-to-end for small chat models; p99 target for critical flows <= 400ms.
- Reserved capacity ask: baseline reserved pool to cover 70% peak with burstable on-demand for 30% (business prefers predictable monthly commit). Initial ask = 16x A100-equivalent GPUs; Redwood to provide mapping and packing strategy.
- Warm pools: need explicit warm-pool behavior for KV cache and tokenizers (avoid 2-4s cold starts). Want options: always-on warm pool for critical routes, and pre-warm windowing for events (60–120s).
- Autoscaling policies: prefer predictable scale-up (fast; <30s to add serving capacity for replicas) and conservative scale-down (cooldown >= 5m) to avoid cache churn. Explore hybrid policy: instant pod add + staged cache join.
- Queueing behavior: require bounded request queue depth per-route and backpressure semantics; want circuit-breaker to fail fast vs long tail build-up. POC logs showed queuing spikes in 95-99th percentiles during synthetic burst tests.

Security & procurement notes:
- Must pass internal SOC/ISO questionnaire; KMS integration mandatory. Data residency constraint for EU wallets subset. Procurement wants SLA with financial penalty tiering (p95/p99 breaches).

Commercial negotiation positions discussed:
- Verdigris prefers a 12-month reserved commitment with monthly true-up; looking for price protection and a transparent warm-pool pricing model (charge only for memory-resident warm workers vs full GPU-hour billing).
- They asked about ability to pause capacity for non-business hours (nightly window) without losing reserved discounts.

Open technical risks and follow-ups:
- Validate scale-up latency under realistic large-model KV sizes (customer has long context sessions ~12k tokens).
- Confirm how routing fallback to smaller quantized variants impacts user-facing latency and cost math. Need Redwood to produce sample cost/latency curves for their traffic mix.
- Need clarification on autoscaler hysteresis: what telemetry is used (gpu_util, queue_length, tail_latency) and how to tune thresholds for minimal oscillation.

Decision criteria (internal to Verdigris):
- Predictable monthly OPEX within 10% forecast error;
- P95 chat latency <= 200ms in production-like load;
- Clear, auditable fallbacks + tracing (for compliance)

Next tactical steps:
- Redwood to deliver updated POC runbooks + results from synthetic burst run (action: Daniel, due 2026-03-05).
- Draft SLA redline sent to Verdigris legal (Marisol to coordinate; target 2026-03-12).
- Procurement to confirm NDA & budget line (Verdigris) — blocker until signed.
